note: Former/popular names for a ground we already carry under a different (current/official) name. Each entry points straight at the ground's own id -- never a name substring -- so a search never has to guess between two grounds that happen to share a word (see the app note on 'Achter de Kazerne' below). Consumed by the CSV importer's ground matching (src/data/store.ts); NOT the same list as GROUND_NICKNAMES (fan search-as-you-type + OCR ticket scanning), which is matched by name substring and would be ambiguous for some of these.

aliases.name: AFAS Stadion
aliases.source: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q649755 -- KV Mechelen's ground; "Achter de Kazerne" is its pre-sponsorship name. Not added to GROUND_NICKNAMES: a bare "AFAS Stadion" substring search also hits AZ's ground in Alkmaar, which sorts first on capacity.

aliases.name: Versluys Arena
aliases.source: KV Oostende's ground, renamed since "Albertpark Stadion"; matched to our own grounds-be.json row by name (Versluys Arena, Oostende).

aliases.name: Stade de Rocourt
aliases.source: RFC de Liège/RFC Liège's ground, still on the same site; "Vélodrome de Rocourt" was its name while it doubled as a cycling track.

aliases.name: Stade de Rocourt
aliases.source: Same ground as "stade velodrome de rocourt" above.

aliases.name: Stade Hubert Freson
aliases.source: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q15694367 (Stade du Pairay, RFC Seraing's ground, 50.6004,5.50372) is 22 m from our osm-way-154514015 "Stade Hubert Freson" row -- the same stadium under its popular vs. its official/OSM name.

aliases.name: RheinEnergieSTADION
aliases.source: Same Wikidata item (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q151893, inception 1921) as today's RheinEnergieStadion -- treated as one continuously-redeveloped ground, not a move to a different site (judgment call; see historic-grounds.json note for 1. FC Köln).

aliases.name: Stade Roi Baudouin - Koning Boudewijnstadion
aliases.source: Belgium's national stadium was called Heizelstadion before the 1985 Heysel disaster; rebuilt on the same site and renamed Koning Boudewijnstadion/Stade Roi Baudouin. Also findable via the bilingual-name-halves matching added alongside this file, since our own row already carries both languages.

aliases.name: Cegeka Arena
aliases.source: KRC Genk's ground grew out of Waterschei THOR's old André Dumontstadion, renamed Thyl Gheyselinckstadion 1990-1999 after a new main stand, later redeveloped again into today's Cegeka Arena -- one site, not a move (judgment call, no Wikidata item for the old name; see https://www.stadiumguide.com/cristalarena/ and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cegeka_Arena). historic-grounds.json carries no separate spell for KRC Genk for the same reason.

aliases.name: Cegeka Arena
aliases.source: Same ground as "thyl gheyselinckstadion" above, its earlier name still.

aliases.name: Elindus Arena
aliases.source: SV Zulte Waregem's ground, renamed from Regenboogstadion (sponsor renames since).
